utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you, according to this statement that we were provided a short time ago, you are a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina, also hold citizenship in the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long have you been a citizen of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Since 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you go obtaining that citizenship?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I obtained all the necessary documents for citizenship to be granted me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you apply for this citizenship?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I gave the power of attorney to my aunt who lived in Banja Luka to -- who lived in Zagreb, I'm sorry, to present the papers in my name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you first become a member of the HDZ political party?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So about the time that the party was first established; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during what time did you serve as treasurer of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: The period, well, not throughout, but I was the secretary for a time and in 1991, 1992, the treasurer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you stop being treasurer of the HDZ, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you held that position essentially throughout the armed conflict with the Muslims; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Except for the time when there was combat during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But just in terms of the dates, and I won't belabour this other than this final question, you indicated -- I believe your testimony was, sir, that you held that position starting sometime in 1991, 1992 and continued in that position until sometime in 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to being treasurer, there was a time, was there not, when you were the secretary of the HDZ party in Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember, sir, attending a meeting, a large meeting of the HDZ/HVO leadership in Travnik in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I did not attend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not. All right. Were you the secretary of the Vitez HDZ at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't recall -- well, sir, let me just ask you...

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher could put before the witness Exhibit Z2631 with the witness having the B/C/S version in front of him and the English being put on the ELMO, please. I apologise for the short notice to the usher, but unfortunately we are all operating under short notice concerning this witness. Your Honour, forgive me, it may have been mismarked or it may be 631. The marking looks like a "2" but it is a "Z". My mistake, Z631. Yes, if the witness could be shown the B/C/S version and the English version put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I show this to you only to see if it might refresh your recollection. These are the minutes of a meeting in Travnik on the 8th of April 1993, being described in the first paragraph under the date as minutes taken at the meeting of the presidents and vice-presidents of municipal HVOs, et cetera, et cetera, secretaries of municipal boards. And if I could -- and I'm not sure, I can't tell you whether the B/C/S pages correspond exactly, but if you would turn to -- I'll see if it does -- if you will turn to the second page of the B/C/S version, and for the Court and counsel, the third page of the English, the top of the third page of the English version, I guess, for the ELMO. Do you see there, sir, that there is - admittedly the spelling of the last name is T-i-b-o-l-a, otherwise, without the -- except for the A, your last name, and your first name located there, described as, in fact, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the secretary of the Vitez HDZ. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, allowing for the possibility that it could, in fact, be a different name or it could be a typing error, does this refresh your recollection that you were, in fact, at this meeting on the 8th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I did not attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recall getting notice of it? Do you recall anything about the circumstances of that meeting being called apparently by a steering committee including, on the first page, Colonel Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I am not aware of this meeting, and I was not present at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, sir, very briefly, can you tell the Court what banks, the names of the banks that you have been employed at in that -- since about 1992. You've mentioned various banks experience, especially in part two of your statement, but it's not exactly clear. You mentioned at -- let me start over again, please, forgive me. You mentioned, for instance, that one time you were a bank clerk in something called the -- I'll probably pronounce this wrong -- Zagrebacka Banka BiH. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: That's where I am now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what banks then, using that as an example, can you just give to the Court the names of the banks where you have been employed during, let's say during the 1992, 1993, 1994 time period?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: The first bank I worked for was the Privredna Banka Sarajevo in Travnik, and branch office Vitez. When that bank was reorganised, the Privredna Banka of Travnik was set up and the branch office in Vitez. When I left the Privredna Banka Travnik, I moved to the Croatian bank of Mostar in Mostar, and I am now in the Zagrebacka Banka BH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992, I left the Privredna Banka or commercial bank of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: In April, the Croatian Bank of Mostar was established in 1993 and a month or a month and a half ago, the Zagrebacka Banka of BH was established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just now? Just a month and a half ago now; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, my question to you is: What does it mean that this was -- this bank that you joined that was based in Mostar, it was the Croatian bank. In what sense can you tell the Court was it a Croatian bank as opposed to a Bosnian bank or a Yugoslavian bank? How was it a Croatian bank?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: The bank is a bank, but its name was that. That was what its name was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did it have an association with perhaps a banking company or a financial institution in Croatia or in Zagreb, or why the name Croatian bank?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: That bank was founded with the re-organisation of the Privredna Banka or commercial bank of Zagreb, and it was an independent autonomous bank in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you is this: Since that one bank, the bank in Travnik was reorganised, as you've told us about, is it fair to say that ever since that time, all the banks which you have been employed at have been, using your terminology, banks called Croatian banks or banks with a home office or their base in Croatia or in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: The Privredna Banka of Zagreb had its head office in Zagreb. The Hrvatska Bank of Mostar in Mostar, the Zagrebacka Banka also now has its headquarters in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that bank in Mostar then established again?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Which bank?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one that we have been discussing as the Croatian bank, the Bank of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: On the 1st of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us a lot about the financial currency situation in Bosnia during 1992 and 1993. Let me ask you, if some additional or alternative currency was needed with the breakup of the former Yugoslavia, why didn't you just continue - not just you, but the Croat community in general, and others - why did you not just continue using the Deutschemark, which by all accounts was in circulation and widely used? Why did you not simply continue using the Deutschemark as opposed to introducing the Croatian state currency?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: There weren't enough German marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These Croatian dinars, which later became kuna, where was this currency printed?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: The Croatian dinar, in the Croatian state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did this currency come into circulation, then? How was it brought to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Through trade. If somebody wanted to purchase goods, they had to take German marks with them. In Croatia there was a decision taken that you couldn't trade with German marks, that all currencies had to be exchanged for the Croatian dinar. So that those who had some Croatian dinars left took them back with them to Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it not a fact that in addition to whatever currency may have come into -- that is, Croatian currency that may have come into the country of Bosnia through trade, that in fact the substantial majority of that currency came into Bosnia by large shipments of currency, simply shipped and put into circulation from Croatia, put into circulation in Bosnia; isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The vouchers that you have discussed, in reality, is it not true, sir, that these were vouchers that were created and carried out or used under the supervision and control of the central BiH government; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: No. The vouchers were printed by the banks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, my question wasn't how they were printed. But wasn't that system put into place under the supervision and control of the legitimate central government of BiH, Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. And that money in time became obsolete because you couldn't trade with them, or lost value.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that during the time that first the Croatian dinar and then later the kuna began to be used in Bosnia, that that itself was a new currency? It was something that had only been created in Croatia, at least most recently, around that same time, in 1992; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. The Croatian dinars came from Croatia later, and they were worth something because you could purchase goods with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I understand, sir. But my question to you is this: The Croatian dinar was itself a new and, at the time, untested currency, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: It was just used in the area of Hrvatska, on the territory of Croatia, and it was a transition from the Yugoslav dinar to the Croatian dinar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement - I guess you don't have it in front of you, but for the Court and counsel, I'm looking at paragraph 3.5 - there's a statement that says: "At the same time in Croatia, the national currency (Croatian dinar, later replaced with a kuna) became stronger." Now, when you say "at the same time," can you tell us what time you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Unless I'm mistaken, it was 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was the first time that that currency had been established, even in Croatia. Unless perhaps there was some other historical usage. But in modern times, is it not the case that that was a brand new currency, first introduced by the Croatian government in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the interest of time, I'll simply refer to some documents and put the question to the witness in this way:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Court has in evidence, and the witness can be told, Exhibit Z134.1, about the introduction of the Croatian dinar in Kiseljak municipality on the 15th of June, 1992; Z134.2, again about the use of dinars in June 1992; Exhibit Z341.6, a decree of Herceg-Bosna on the 22nd of September, 1992 about transactions in Croatian dinars; and there's others. But I think the point can be made this way: Sir, isn't it true that the imposition or establishment of the use of the Croatian dinar in Bosnia around, approximately, the middle of 1992 was about at the same time that that currency was first created in Croatia; and in fact, its introduction into Bosnia was essentially part of a nationalistic policy?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicate, sir, in paragraph 3.6, that in fact by the latter part of 1992, the Central Bosnian government in Sarajevo had established the BiH dinar, and at the end of that paragraph, 3.6, you state: "At the end of 1992 and in the beginning of 1993, the BiH dinar started to circulate also in other parts of the BiH. All the currencies mentioned above were in use at that time." Is that correct? Do you stand by that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: At the end of 1992, the BH dinar appeared as well, and it was exchanged against the Yugoslav dinar, so that all currencies existed in 1992 and were in use. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the situation that existed at that time, then, at least by late 1992, in terms of currency in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was that, one, there was the Deutschemark, which had been widely circulated and used for some time by all ethnic groups; secondly, there was the officially established currency of the government, of the legitimate government, in Sarajevo; and those currencies both were in circulation and in use; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: The currency from Sarajevo couldn't be used because you couldn't exchange it for goods. It was only used in the territory of Central Bosnia if people wanted to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 3.6 you said: "... initially circulated in Sarajevo, Zenica, Bihac, and Tuzla," and at the end of that paragraph, you say, "... it also was circulating in other parts of BiH. All the currencies ... were in use." Now, is that the truth?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: The times and periods when the BH dinars were distributed into the towns, from Bihac to Sarajevo, I couldn't really tell you how that was done. However, on the territory of Central Bosnia, that currency appeared at the end of 1992 and it was in circulation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, that there was various legislation enacted by the Herceg-Bosna government, if you will, in Mostar, creating such things as custom duties, creating such things as taxes, all of which were stated in terms of Croatian dinars for purposes of collecting these taxes, duties, and custom excises?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes, because the Croatian dinar appeared before the BH dinar did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, are you suggesting that there was a time when the Herceg-Bosna government withdrew that policy and said, "Well, we won't use Croatian dinars anymore because now we have a national currency," the Bosnia-Herzegovina government?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: That came later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll come to that momentarily. Sir, I'll put it to you again, isn't it a fact that the use of the Croatian dinar, later the kuna, was a policy decision heavily personally endorsed and promoted by President Tudjman in Zagreb and passed on, if you will, through his directions and the arms of the HDZ political party to be also implemented in at least the Herceg-Bosna parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina as an indication of statehood?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I must answer no to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would disagree. If President Tudjman was described as having stated that the use of the kuna was an important expression of the Croatian nation-building process, would you disagree with that statement then?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes. I cannot agree with it because all the documents that we used were entitled the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you tell me some -- can you point to us, sir, can you -- more importantly not to me, but the Court, any document in which the legitimate government of Bosnia-Herzegovina accepted the Croatian dinar as legitimate currency to be used on its territory? You just said that it was done by the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can you point us, sir, to any acceptance of Croatian dinar currency as legitimate currency by that government?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: In the Dayton Agreements, the following currencies were used: The kuna, the German mark and the Bosnian dinar. They were legal tender on the territory of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand the Dayton Agreement, sir, at least parts of it. But that was not my question. Can you point the Judges, can you point the Court to any documentation, any legislation, any decisions by the central government in Sarajevo accepting and saying, "We accept the Croatian dinar as one of the official currencies on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina." That's my question.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: The central government in Sarajevo forgot that Central Bosnia existed. The documents from the central government, we did not receive any documents from the central government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Do you recall a time when the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina declared this entity Herceg-Bosna, first the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and later the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, that the constitutional court declared those entities unconstitutional? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also recall that, as part of those decisions, the use of the Croatian dinar was also ruled invalid and not a legitimate currency?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I don't want you to replace these. The Croatian dinar existed in Central Bosnia and was used just like every other currency. There was no order that any particular and sole currency be used exclusively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just repeat my last question, sir, and then we'll move on, I'm almost finished. The question to you is this: Do you know that the decision of the constitutional court not only invalidated the entity Herceg-Bosna but invalidated the use of the Croatian dinar? And either you know or you don't know. It's a simple question; if you don't know you just say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it not the case that, even after the creation of the Muslim/Croat Federation, the Croat part of that Federation, or at least some parts of it, continued to resist and refused to recognise the Bosnia-Herzegovina dinar as legitimate currency in the territory of what was claimed to be Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: All currencies were in circulation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Obrad Piljak?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in October 1994, was he the governor of the Muslim/Croat Federation National Bank?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I cannot answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you have any recollection that on about the 4th of October, 1994, Mr. Piljak took the position that the Bosnia-Herzegovina dinar had no chance of becoming the official currency of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and that the only currency that would be recognised on the territory of Herceg-Bosna was the Croatian kuna and the German mark?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Honours, I have to interfere because this question goes beyond the time frame notified by the indictment and also goes beyond the scope of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can just respond briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution's point is that that was a continuation in one and the same policy that had been in place since at least 1992. The witness himself a few moments ago made a reference to Dayton. The Prosecution's point is this was a continuous unbroken policy that, even after Dayton, the Bosnian Croat position was that they would not recognise the BH dinar. I ask it only for that final purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Tibold, you've heard what the Prosecutor says. Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I do not. The people of Central Bosnia was economically depleted and recognised only the currency which they could use to buy their basic necessities. Any travel with the Bosnian dinar ended up in the territory of Herzegovina. You could go no further with that currency, not to mention Croatia or Europe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The final question: Sir, I put it to you that, in fact, that is not the case that. I'll give you one more chance to respond to this. I put it to you that that was not the case, that it continued to be the case that the Bosnian Croat part of the Federation that they would not - I mean, eventually they may have, but in 1994 they continued to refuse to recognise the Bosnia-Herzegovinian dinar on the territory of Herceg-Bosna as any official currency; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: No, it is not. I have to answer this. The central government in Sarajevo, after Dayton, was to correct the amount of dinars in the territory of Federation, but this was never done. And that is why this dinar could not be widely embraced. I wouldn't say that it wasn't in circulation; it was. It replaced the convertible mark which is now in use in -- throughout the Federation and there are no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Your Honours. Re-examined by Mr. Mikulicic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tibold, you were asked what bank you worked for at present and you told us Zagrebacka Banka, Zagreb Bank BH. Is it true that Zagrebacka Banka is an international banking institution which is quoted on the London Stock Exchange?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that Zagrebacka Banka has its branches in different countries, not Croatia alone?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For a while, you work for Privredna Banka Zagreb, Zagreb Commercial Bank. It is also true that it had its branches in various European countries and in the United States?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also worked for Hrvatska Banka, Croatian Bank Shareholding Society Mostar. Did this bank come from Croatia or did it originate in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: That bank is Bosnia-Herzegovinian bank, that is, it originated in the Federation, and it covered the area from Tuzla, Sarajevo, Travnik, Bihac. All the pensions from Croatia or Europe were paid through our bank as of 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. It was put to you, Mr. Tibold, that the central government in Sarajevo had organised the printing of vouchers that you told us about. If that were so, would those vouchers be valid throughout the BH and not only the territory of some towns?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Quite so, and it is proof that banks were autonomous, or rather that it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or rather that it was not organised by the central government, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today, convertible mark is broadly or generally-accepted legal tender in the Federation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In all the other currencies that were in circulation in that area, have they been invalidated or are they still in circulation?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Except for the Yu dinar, the others are in circulation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it mean that in Central Bosnia, the Croatian kuna is still in circulation there?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the German mark?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does the federal government try to put an end to the circulation of those two currencies?

utterances.speaker: ZDENKO TIBOLD
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tibold. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That concludes your evidence, Mr. Tibold. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, we'll have your next witness tomorrow, and that will be the last one this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You have, I hope, a full programme for the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Hopefully we do. I mean, so far we don't have any information that somebody is having a problem or something. We've added a couple of reserves, so even if somebody is not appearing, we will have reserves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you should, if you can, have at least ten available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: That's exactly what we demanded. Indeed, I think we demanded 11, if I'm not wrong now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. We'll adjourn now until half past nine tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of September, 2000, at 9.30 a.m. 23 24 25 Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.
